title: CS2103T Review — Bernard Teo Zhi Yi
description: This module is the first group software project for computer science students. For most computer science students, this module is twinned with CS2101. CS2103T is the twinned version of this module, while CS2103 is the non-twinned version. Lectures and exams are combined and they are identical for CS2103 and CS2103T students. However, CS2103T students form project groups with other CS2103T students only, because the same project group is required for CS2101. The main reference material for this module is on this website (). There are two parts to this module — the lectures (which closely follow the reference website) and the group project. For most students, the group project takes up the bulk of time spent on this module. The address book application is written in Java, and students will only be graded on the Java code that they have written. Being sufficiently acquainted with the main reference material (the CS2103/T website) will allow you to do well for finals.

title: CS2103 Software Engineering | Module Reviews
description: This module teaches the basics of software engineering and how to work together as a team to deliver a software product. Finally, there is a project that runs for the second half of the module which will allow you to apply the concepts taught in the module in a team setting. It is also the first module that requires students to work together as a team to deliver a software project at the end of the semester. For the first half of the semester before the group project starts, there is another individual project that is also written in Java and is aimed to get students familiar with the IDE and code base provided by the lecturer. The tutorials itself are the most chill component of the module, as everyone will be seated down together to talk about the project and some basic software engineering principles. **Project workload**: Extremely high, with an individual project during the first half of the semester and a group project during the second half of the semester.

It does not affect most people, but it does make it unfair for the minorities in the class (the smaller gender group in the class, foreigners, minority race in the class, etc.) as they will be thrown around by other teams and they basically have zero right to pick their desired group. 2.   If you code more, you're more likely to get lesser marks due to the nature of PE. Sure, if you are a good coder you should have avoided some of the more obvious bugs. And guess what, if that bug is caught, it's on you coz you coded the thing, not on your other teammates because they don't have the skills to code some of the more critical things. It's so absurd that the mark depends on which team you get to review and which people reviewed your project.
